section: Sustainable development - definition, Brundtland Report, SDGs and India's progress
subsections: First definition and milestones; Brundtland Report
Related concepts - carrying capacity, Earth Overshoot Day, intergenerational equity

accepted.s:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:
A. Adoption of Agenda 2030
B. Rio Earth Summit
C. Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment
D. Johannesburg World Summit on Sustainable Development
accepted.x: The Stockholm Conference was held in 1972, the Rio Earth Summit in 1992, the Johannesburg Summit in 2002 and Agenda 2030 was adopted in 2015.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last milestones, then place the intermediate events by year.
accepted.sec: First definition and milestones; Brundtland Report

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Johannesburg World Summit on Sustainable Development was held in 2002, also known as Rio+10. Stockholm was held in 1972, Rio+20 in 2012 and Agenda 2030 was adopted in 2015.
accepted.tq: Check the year-event pairing and reject swapped milestone years.
accepted.sec: First definition and milestones; Brundtland Report

accepted.s: The decision to develop the Sustainable Development Goals was taken at which event?
accepted.x: The 2012 Rio+20 Conference, formally the United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development, took the decision to develop the SDGs.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the closely related Rio, Rio+10 and Rio+20 milestones.
accepted.sec: First definition and milestones; Brundtland Report

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT an outcome associated with the 1992 Rio Earth Summit?
o: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
accepted.x: The SDGs were developed after the 2012 Rio+20 Conference and adopted in 2015. Agenda 21, the CBD and the UNFCCC are associated with the 1992 Rio Earth Summit.
accepted.tq: Find the later milestone among outcomes of the 1992 summit.
accepted.sec: First definition and milestones; Brundtland Report

accepted.s: The Brundtland Commission was chaired by:
accepted.x: The World Commission on Environment and Development was chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland, who was the Prime Minister of Norway.
accepted.tq: Use the person-title and country association to identify the chairperson.
accepted.sec: First definition and milestones; Brundtland Report

accepted.s: The Sustainable Development Goals were adopted by the United Nations General Assembly during its:
accepted.x: The SDGs were adopted at the 70th session of the UN General Assembly as part of the 2030 Agenda.
accepted.tq: Apply the numerical-session distinction instead of confusing it with the adoption year.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sustainable Development Goals:
1. There are 17 goals.
2. They contain 169 targets.
3. Their implementation period is 2015–2030.
4. They came into force from 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The SDG framework consists of 17 goals and 169 targets, covers 2015–2030, and came into force from 2016.
accepted.tq: Verify each numerical and temporal statement independently before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: How many global indicators are associated with the Sustainable Development Goals?
accepted.x: The global SDG framework has 232 indicators. The figures 169, 277 and 113 relate respectively to targets, India’s National Indicator Framework 2026 and the SDG India Index 2023–24.
accepted.tq: Separate goals, targets and indicators before choosing the figure.

accepted.s: India’s National Indicator Framework 2026 contains how many indicators?
accepted.x: India’s National Indicator Framework 2026 contains 277 indicators and is associated with the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the national indicator framework from the global indicator framework and the SDG India Index.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Millennium Development Goals?
accepted.x: The MDGs consisted of 8 goals for the period 2000–2015. They preceded and provided roots for the SDGs.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the MDG and SDG goal counts and time periods.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer:
List-I (SDG number)
A. 4
B. 7
C. 12
D. 16

List-II (Theme)
i. Responsible Consumption and Production
ii. Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
iii. Quality Education and lifelong learning
iv. Affordable and Clean Energy
accepted.x: SDG 4 concerns quality education, SDG 7 affordable and clean energy, SDG 12 responsible consumption and production, and SDG 16 peace, justice and strong institutions.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure goal-theme pair and eliminate codes that disturb it.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the grouping of the Sustainable Development Goals is correct?
o: Goals 8–10 deal exclusively with environmental protection.
Goals 1–7 extend the Millennium Development Goals.
The last seven goals deal only with poverty eradication.
accepted.x: Goals 1–7 extend the MDG concerns. Goals 8–10 cover jobs, infrastructure and distribution, while the last seven focus on sustainability.
accepted.tq: Use the broad grouping of consecutive goal numbers to reject overexclusive descriptions.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the three pillars of sustainability?
accepted.x: The three pillars are economic growth, social inclusion or equity, and environmental protection. Military strength is not a pillar of sustainability.
accepted.tq: Identify the outsider against the standard three-pillar framework.

accepted.s: Sustainable development requires the three pillars of sustainability to be:
o: Balanced without maximising any one pillar in isolation
Ranked with economic growth above all other considerations
accepted.x: Sustainable development seeks a balance among economic growth, social inclusion and environmental protection rather than maximising one pillar alone.
accepted.tq: Apply the balancing principle to a policy situation instead of selecting a single-pillar approach.

accepted.s: Which of the following represents a socio-environmental overlap?
o: A policy concerning only political representation
A policy combining military strength and economic growth
A policy combining only industrial output and profits
A policy combining social inclusion and environmental protection
accepted.x: The socio-environmental overlap combines social concerns with environmental protection. The three recognised overlaps include socio-economic, socio-environmental and eco-environmental dimensions.
accepted.tq: Break the compound term into its two component sustainability pillars.

accepted.s: The basic goal of sustainable development is to:
o: Maximise present profits regardless of future effects
Exploit all available resources before they become scarce
Meet present needs while preserving choices for future generations
Suspend economic development until environmental degradation ends
accepted.x: The core goal is to meet present needs without reducing the options available to future generations, within the Earth’s carrying capacity.
accepted.tq: Reject extreme present-only and growth-denial options and apply the intergenerational principle.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Agenda 2030:
1. It is universal in application.
2. Its goals are interconnected.
3. It follows the principle of leaving no one behind.
4. It is based on inclusive participation and partnerships.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Agenda 2030 is universal, interconnected, inclusive and participatory, and is guided by the principle of leaving no one behind.
accepted.tq: Treat the comprehensive option as correct when each listed principle belongs to the agenda.

accepted.s: The principle that Agenda 2030 applies to developed, developing and least developed countries alike is known as its:
accepted.x: Universality means that Agenda 2030 applies to all countries, irrespective of their level of development.
accepted.tq: Match the exact principle with its defining scope rather than a related development term.

accepted.s: The Agenda 2030 framework is guided by which of the following human-rights instruments?
o: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species alone
accepted.x: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, along with international human-rights treaties, guides the Agenda 2030 framework.
accepted.tq: Identify the human-rights foundation rather than an environmental treaty.

accepted.s: Agenda 2030 places particular emphasis on ending all discrimination and violence against:
accepted.x: A specific focus of Agenda 2030 is ending all discrimination and violence against women and girls.
accepted.tq: Read the scope of the focus group precisely and avoid narrowing or broadening it without basis.

accepted.s: The two principal roots of Agenda 2030 are:
o: The World Trade Organization and the International Monetary Fund
The Kyoto Protocol and the Montreal Protocol
The Millennium Development Goals and the Rio+20 outcome
The Stockholm Convention and the Paris Agreement
accepted.x: Agenda 2030 grew from the Millennium Development Goals and the outcome of the Rio+20 Conference.
accepted.tq: Link the agenda to its stated development and conference antecedents.

accepted.s: Carrying capacity refers to:
o: The total quantity of minerals in the Earth’s crust
The maximum population an environment can support indefinitely without degradation
The annual rate of economic growth of a country
The maximum number of industries a city can legally establish
accepted.x: Carrying capacity is the maximum population that an environment can support indefinitely without degradation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an ecological population concept from resource stocks and economic measures.
accepted.sec: Related concepts - carrying capacity, Earth Overshoot Day, intergenerational equity

accepted.s:
The concern regarding the Earth’s finite carrying capacity is associated with which of the following works or events?
1. Limits to Growth
2. Our Common Future
3. United Nations Conference on Environment and Development, 1992
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The finite carrying capacity of the Earth is a concern reflected in Limits to Growth, Our Common Future and the 1992 UNCED process.
accepted.tq: Use the comprehensive option when all three listed references address the same ecological limit.
accepted.sec: Related concepts - carrying capacity, Earth Overshoot Day, intergenerational equity

accepted.s: Earth Overshoot Day is the date on which:
o: The global temperature first exceeds a fixed legal limit
Humanity’s annual demand on nature exceeds the Earth’s regeneration capacity for that year
The Earth completes one full cycle around the Sun
All countries formally adopt their annual environmental budgets
accepted.x: Earth Overshoot Day marks the point when humanity’s demand on nature in a year exceeds what the Earth can regenerate during that year.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise demand-versus-regeneration relationship in the definition.
accepted.sec: Related concepts - carrying capacity, Earth Overshoot Day, intergenerational equity

accepted.s: Earth Overshoot Day is computed by the:
accepted.x: The Global Footprint Network computes Earth Overshoot Day. Plastic Overshoot Day is an analogous concept relating specifically to plastic use.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-ownership trap and distinguish the ecological organisation from economic bodies.
accepted.sec: Related concepts - carrying capacity, Earth Overshoot Day, intergenerational equity

accepted.s: Which of the following principles was NOT endorsed at the 1992 Rio process?
accepted.x: The precautionary principle, polluter pays principle and common but differentiated responsibilities were endorsed at Rio 1992. Unrestricted resource exploitation is contrary to sustainable development.
accepted.tq: Find the policy principle that contradicts the Rio sustainability framework.
accepted.sec: Related concepts - carrying capacity, Earth Overshoot Day, intergenerational equity

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with a 2015 Agenda 2030 milestone?
o: Adopted on 5 June 1992 at Rio de Janeiro
Adopted on 25 September 2015 at New York
accepted.x: Agenda 2030 was adopted on 25 September 2015 in New York. The other dates and places do not correspond to its adoption.
accepted.tq: Combine the exact date and venue to defeat swapped conference details.
accepted.sec: First definition and milestones; Brundtland Report
